title: Join types: inner vs left

cells.text: Last lesson every game found its studio. But what about studios with no games in our table? This lesson shows how merge decides which rows to keep.

cells.prompt: Press Run to load games and studios. Valve and Ubisoft are in studios, but no game in our table has their studio_id.
cells.code:
import pandas as pd
games = pd.read_csv("games.csv")
studios = pd.read_csv("studios.csv")
studios

cells.text: By default, merge() only keeps rows that match in **both** tables. That's called an **inner** join, so Valve and Ubisoft disappear. With `how="left"`, merge keeps **every** row from the first (left) table, even with no match, and fills the missing columns with **NaN**.

cells.prompt: Studios is first now. Nintendo has 4 games, and Valve and Ubisoft have none but are kept anyway. How many rows will this have? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: 15 matching games, plus 1 row each for Valve and Ubisoft with NaN where the game columns would be.

cells.prompt: Replace ___ with "left" (in quotes) to keep every studio, even ones with no games, then press Run.
hints: The value is text, so it needs quotes.

cells.text: That's how analysts find what's missing: do a left join, then look for NaN with `isna()`.

cells.prompt: Your turn: find the studios with no games in our table. Store the left join in m, then show just the studio_name column of the rows where title is NaN.
hints: Line 1: m = the left join. Line 2: filter m[m["title"].isna()], then pick [["studio_name"]].

cells.prompt: Count the games for every studio, including studios with 0 games. Group m by studio_name and count() the title column (count() skips NaN, so Valve gets 0).
hints: Use m from the cell above.

cells.prompt: Which table you write first matters, because that's the one that keeps all its rows. This time games is first. How many rows? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: Every game has a studio, so keeping all games gives 15 rows. Valve and Ubisoft aren't kept, because studios is now the second (right) table.

recap: An inner join (the default) keeps only matches. how="left" keeps every row of the first table and fills gaps with NaN. A left join plus isna() finds what's missing.
